articles.description:
Most support bots have the same problem: they forget everything.
You can talk to them for an hour, come back the next day, and the entire conversation might as well have never happened. Every session starts from zero. Every problem must be re-explained. From a systems perspective, most of these bots are just stateless request processors pretending to be conversational systems.
I ran into this problem while building a support automation system, and the fix turned out to be less about better prompting and more about something much simpler: memory.
Specifically, persistent agent memory.
Once I added that piece, the system stopped behaving like a goldfish.

articles.description:
SvelteKit Port: 32.50 kB Gzip, +72% Over Plain Svelte — Meta-Framework Tax, Round Two



Plain Svelte 5 shipped at 18.92 kB. SvelteKit on the exact same spec ships at 32.50 kB — a +72% regression for adding a meta-framework over the same core. The consolation: at 32.50 kB it's still −33% smaller than React. Meta-framework tax is real across ecosystems; Svelte's base is just small enough to absorb it.
Entry #6 in the framework comparison series. The previous entry on Nuxt established the "meta-framework tax" pattern — Vue 28.76 kB → Nuxt 52.01 kB, a +81% jump. SvelteKit shows the same pattern: Svelte 18.92 kB → SvelteKit 32.50 kB, +72%. Different ecosystem, same phenomenon.

articles.author: Dev Rajput
articles.description:
As I stood at the crossroads of code and existential dread, the city outside my window began to stir, oblivious to the battle raging within. The whisky hangover had long worn off, replaced by the adrenaline-fueled highs of tackling a massive workload and the quiet lows of confronting the abyss. I had knocked out the bulk of my office work, but the real challenge lay in the Soul in Motion engine, where the pursuit of automation and innovation beckoned.
In the midst of integrating APIs and crunching code, I found myself at the mercy of that familiar, haunting feeling - the sense of being completely alone. It's a specter that threatens to derail even the most focused of minds, and I'm no exception. But I refused to be swayed, to be an object of pity or sympathy. Instead, I drew on a deep well of determination, straightened my back, and forced myself back into the fray.
The code began to flow once more, as I tackled the APIs of Dev.to and Hashnode, each platform falling like a domino as I pushed forward. Three down, six to go. And then, just as momentum was building, the Claude weekly limit kicked in, slamming the brakes on my progress. It was a harsh reminder that even the most relentless among us must sometimes yield to the constraints of the world. As I stepped back, eyes burning from the screen, I couldn't help but wonder: what lies beyond the wall that I've hit, and what will it take to break through? The darkness closes in, and I'm left with only one thought: the real test is not in the code, but in the silence that follows.
articles.title: Soul in Motion — 06:00 PM | 2026-04-12
